transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording ended at ~14:48)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marcus Reed (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (Redrock - Head of AI); Tom Willis (Redrock - Infra Lead); Priya Gupta (Redrock - Security); Dan Rivera (Redrock - PM)

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on Dedicated / reserved GPU capacity for Redrock's inference serving. Primary concerns: isolation and compliance, predictable throughput for peak trading windows, burst strategy for unexpected spikes, autoscale and rollback behavior, and integration with Redrock's VPC and KMS. Agreed next steps: pricing, SOC2 + network docs, schedule benchmarking session next week.

Topics: dedicated capacity, reserved GPUs, VPC/private deployment, burst/bursting to hosted, autoscaling policies, latency SLOs vs cost, KMS/encryption, audit logs, rollout plan, benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lena with Redwood, and with me is Marcus our SE. Hey team, how are you doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Good thanks, appreciate you. We wanted to run through how Dedicated would map to our trading inference workloads, mainly around reserved GPUs and how we handle spikes.
[00:18] Marcus: Great, that's exactly what we like to focus on. Quick qualifying q — what's your current model stack and where are you running inference today?
[00:26] Tom: Right now it's a mix; we have some in-house Llama2 variants on EC2/GPU instances and a small managed endpoint on OpenAI for prototyping. Majority of production is on our own k8s clusters with NVIDIA A100s.
[00:38] Aisha: We're seeing big spikes during market open and earnings windows, like 3–5x baseline for short periods, latency needs to be sub-300ms for our most latency-sensitive flows.
[00:47] Lena: Sub-300ms at tail — understood. When you say spikes 3–5x, is that sustained for minutes, or tens of minutes?
[00:55] Tom: Usually 10–30 minutes for intense events, sometimes up to an hour. We also want predictable cost when that happens, not just sky-high on demand bills.
[01:05] Marcus: Ok makes sense. So Dedicated is a fit: reserved GPU pools give you isolation and predictable throughput. You can also add burst capacity — we offer a managed burst add-on where workloads can overflow to regional hosted capacity under policy. That avoids provisioning double the peak but still gives SLOs.
[01:22] Dan: How does the burst mechanism work? Does it require model replication in both places?
[01:28] Marcus: Yes, you pin compatible model variants. We do background syncs — typically you keep the same quantized variant in Dedicated and a lighter variant in hosted. When Dedicated is saturated, requests route to the hosted pool automatically based on routing policy and latency budget. We also support fallback rules, e.g., degrade to a smaller context length to save tokens.
[01:46] Priya: From security perspective we need to know data residency and encryption in transit and at rest. If requests go to hosted during burst, what about egress and compliance?
[01:56] Lena: Good point. For customers with strict residency needs we recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) rather than hosted bursting. But for many customers there is an acceptable hybrid: burst to hosted only within same region and with a consented data policy. We'll send the SOC2 scope and the data flow diagram.
[02:15] Aisha: Can you share the network topology doc? We need to see how the VPC peering and egress rules look.
[02:19] Marcus: Absolutely — I'll share the private deployment network diagram and the dedicated peering guide. Link: https://redwood.ai/docs/dedicated/network (note: internal link placeholder).
[02:27] Tom: On autoscale — how quickly can you scale up new instances? Our spikes are short so warmup time matters.
[02:34] Marcus: Our Dedicated autoscaler is configurable; we recommend keeping a buffer of warm GPUs for fast bursts. The runtime supports fast warm start for cached KV states and pre-warmed kernels — typical scale-up time from zero can be minutes, but from a warm baseline it's under 30s in many cases. There are also continuous batching strategies to smooth request spikes.
[02:52] Lena: To add, we provide autoscale policies: time-based (market open), metric-based (queue depth), and predictive (cron/event hooks). You can keep a small committed baseline to hit your tail SLOs and let burst handle the rest.
[03:05] Aisha: What's the pricing model for reserved capacity + burst? We want to compare cost vs overprovisioning in-house.
[03:12] Lena: Reserved is monthly commitments for GPU pool — e.g., a 4x A100 pool with an optional burst add-on. The burst add-on is billed separately per-minute at a premium but often cheaper than full overprovisioning. We'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[03:25] Dan: Do you support multiple model versions and can we pin traffic? We need canary rollouts and instant rollback.
[03:31] Marcus: Yes — per-route model pinning, canary rollouts, A/B testing. Rollbacks are instant: the control plane flips routing rules and runtime gracefully drains old instances. We also emit traces for token-level latency which helps root-cause.
[03:46] Priya: About keys — we use AWS KMS and HSM for encryption. Can you integrate with our KMS?
[03:52] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed KMS. For Hosted, we can do envelope encryption with customer keys in some plans but for full control you'd go Private. We'll document the KMS integration steps.
[04:03] Tom: What about audit logs and retention? We need immutable audit trails and session traces for compliance — 1 year retention at minimum.
[04:11] Lena: We emit audit logs (auth events, model version changes, route changes) and can push logs to your SIEM or S3. Retention options are configurable; for Dedicated we can include long-term archive as an add-on.
[04:23] Aisha: Latency/regression monitoring — can you alert on quality regressions after model swaps?
[04:28] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties evals to production prompts. You can set quality gates and get regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We'll show examples in the benchmark session.
[04:38] Dan: For the benchmark next week, what do you need from us?
[04:42] Marcus: Ideally: a representative prompt set (we'll accept anonymized samples), target tail latency and p95 goals, expected concurrency per second during peak, and model weights or container images. Tom, if you can share expected network egress constraints and where the cluster will peer, that helps.
[04:58] Tom: I can get that; I'll share a short doc with concurrency profiles and test endpoints.
[05:03] Priya: One more on encryption: do you support token redaction or PII scrubbing before logs leave the cluster?
[05:09] Marcus: We have built-in redaction hooks and can also run post-processing scrubbing as part of the pipeline. For Private deployments you keep full control; for Hosted bursts we'll agree on redaction policy.
[05:20] Aisha: Any typical gotchas you see with banks switching from self-host to Dedicated?
[05:25] Lena: Mostly around network egress and ACLs, and around lifecycle of model artifacts — making sure the model variants used in burst are functionally equivalent. Also expectation management on autoscale: don't go from zero to production-critical without a warm baseline.
[05:38] Marcus: Another common is tokenization differences between variants; we recommend the same tokenizer and test prompt set.
[05:44] Dan: Ok sounds good. Can you also include an estimate for the SOW and timeline? We want an 8-week pilot to validate during a scheduled earnings window next quarter.
[05:54] Lena: Yes, we'll draft an SOW for an 8-week pilot: setup and config (week 1–2), benchmark runs (week 3), tuning and policy (weeks 4–5), integration and dry runs (weeks 6–7), validation and exit criteria (week 8).
[06:09] Aisha: Perfect. Anything else from your side?
[06:12] Marcus: We'll prepare the benchmark plan and checklist. Expect links to a sample dashboard and the network diagram.
[06:18] Lena: I'll send pricing and security docs. I'll also set up the follow-up meeting for the benchmark run — how's next Tuesday for you all?
[06:26] Tom: Next Tuesday works for me.
[06:28] Priya: Works for security as well.
[06:30] Aisha: Ok set it. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and action items in the next 48 hours.

Meeting End.
